notes: Reviewed and left unchanged: all 11 source and 18 target IDs are partitioned exactly once, every unit is aligned with both heads inside their arrays, and no unrepresented or added unit is needed.

The only materially contested seam is the infinitival 'to' (t011) between μέλλοντες and κρίνεσθαι. I re-checked it and kept the accepted split: rule 7's own examples (ἀντλῆσαι → 'to draw', προσκυνεῖν → 'to worship') and rule 61's no-preposition clause give a bare infinitival marker to its own verb. The competing reading — 'are to' as one periphrasis on μέλλοντες, leaving 'be judged' to the infinitive — remains defensible and is named in the s011 note under rule 16.

'men that are' stays whole on μέλλοντες rather than being split, because no Greek article is present for rules 22, 31, 32 or 90 to operate on; the supplied nominal and relativizer are rule 7 helpers on the participle, exactly as rule 31 says of a relativizer with no article to carry it.

Head on t010 'are' rather than t008 'men' confirmed under rule 91 rather than by English syntax: the corpus spends 'about to' / 'are to' on μέλλω and never 'men', so 'men' is the generic completion rule 17 refuses as a head. This is not a case where the head is in genuine doubt.

νόμου is anarthrous, so 'a' is a rule 7 helper on the noun and rule 51's article clause does not apply; the packet gloss's bracketed '[the]' is projection convention and was not read as a source article. Likewise no article stands to anchor 'of' before ἐλευθερίας, so rule 21's bare-of prohibition keeps it on the noun under rule 23.
